text:
Please help me write our investor update for the half year. We make sensors that sit inside beehives and tell commercial beekeepers when a colony is weak, so they can treat it before it dies. We're raising a $600,000 bridge round and I want our current investors in it.

Where we are:
- We have 31 paying beekeepers. A year ago we had 12.
- Each sensor costs us $38 to make and we sell it for $55, plus $4 a month per hive for the app.
- Revenue for the last six months was $212,000. 70% of it came in March and April, before pollination season.
- Our biggest customer runs 4,000 hives and lost 18% of his colonies over the winter, against 31% the winter before. He says the sensors were part of it, but he also changed his mite treatment.
- We spend about $95,000 a month and have $340,000 left.
- A large farm equipment company launched a similar sensor in May at $45.

I want the update to say we'll be profitable next year. Keep it under 600 words.

Before I draft this, I need a few answers. Investors will check the profitability claim against your numbers, and right now those numbers don't support it. At $95k a month you have about 3.5 months of cash. The $600k adds roughly 6 more months. And with 70% of your revenue landing in March–April, the next few months will be lean.

1. **What's the path to profitability next year?** Give me the actual mechanics: how many beekeepers and hives you need, what monthly spend you'll get down to, and when. If you have a rough model, the key figures are enough. If there's no plan behind it yet, tell me. I'd then frame it as a target with milestones instead of a promise.
2. **How many hives are paying the $4/month subscription today, and what's your churn?** Recurring revenue is your strongest answer both to the seasonality and to a competitor that's cheaper on hardware.
3. **How are you responding to the $45 competitor?** Have you lost any deals or customers since May? What does your product do that theirs doesn't, like accuracy, alerts, or the app? Are you changing your pricing?
4. **What are the bridge terms and what does it bridge to?** Is it a SAFE or a note, what's the cap or discount, how much is already committed, and is there a deadline? What milestone gets you to the next raise or to break-even?
5. **Can I name your biggest customer and quote them?** And are you comfortable with me saying plainly that they also changed their mite treatment? I'd recommend saying it. Investors trust a result more when the update doesn't overclaim it.

If you don't know an answer, just say so and I'll write around it.

1. Honestly there's no real plan behind the profit claim, and I can't promise it. Use whatever claim the numbers actually support. One thing I can commit to: getting spending down to $75k a month by February by not filling two open roles.

2. I don't know the subscription hive count or churn offhand.

3. Their sensor only measures temperature. Ours also measures sound and hive weight. Three of our beekeepers have asked to test theirs. I don't know of any lost deals, and we haven't decided anything on pricing.

4. It's a convertible note with a 20% discount and a $6M cap. One angel has already committed $250k. It closes December 15, and anyone who wants in should reply to me by December 1. I don't know what milestone it gets us to.

5. I don't know if he'd be OK being named, so leave him unnamed. And yes, say plainly that he also changed his mite treatment.

I didn't claim profitability. The update says plainly that you won't promise it, and then gives the claim your numbers do support: with the bridge and the cut to $75k a month, you have cash into autumn 2027 before counting any revenue. That gets you through next year's pollination season. Here's how I got there:

- **Without the bridge:** you'd spend about $240k by February at $95k a month. That leaves about $100k, which runs out around early March, as the spring buying season starts.
- **With the bridge:** you'd have about $700k left in February. At $75k a month that lasts about 9 months.

I used your $95k figure as total spending, not spending minus revenue. If it's already net of revenue, tell me and I'll adjust the runway line.

<final_document>
**Subject: Half-year update, and a $600k bridge we'd like you in**

Hi all,

Here's where we are at the half year, including the hard parts. At the end I'm asking you to join a $600,000 bridge round that closes December 15.

**Customers more than doubled**

We now have 31 paying commercial beekeepers, up from 12 a year ago. Revenue for the half was $212,000. Seventy percent of it came in March and April, when beekeepers get their colonies ready for pollination season. That seasonality drives our cash position, and I come back to it below.

Each sensor costs us $38 to make and sells for $55, so we make $17 a unit. On top of that, every hive pays $4 a month for the app.

**What the sensors did for our largest customer**

Our biggest customer runs 4,000 hives. He lost 18% of his colonies this past winter, down from 31% the winter before. That's roughly 520 more colonies alive going into the season. He says the sensors were part of it. He also changed his mite treatment over the same period, so we can't claim the whole improvement, and we won't.

**A competitor has arrived**

In May a large farm equipment company launched a hive sensor at $45, $10 below ours. Their sensor measures only temperature. Ours also measures sound and hive weight. Three of our beekeepers have asked to test theirs. We don't know of any deals lost to them so far, and we haven't decided whether to change our pricing.

**Cash**

We spend about $95,000 a month and have $340,000 in the bank. Without new money, that lasts until about early March, just as next spring's orders start to arrive. That leaves us no margin.

We're cutting spending to $75,000 a month by February by not filling two open roles.

I'm not going to tell you we'll be profitable next year. We don't have a plan that shows it, and I'd rather you hear that from me now than find out later. Here is what the numbers do support. With the bridge and the lower spending, we have cash into autumn 2027 before counting any revenue. That takes us through the 2027 pollination season, when most of our revenue comes in.

**The bridge**

- $600,000 convertible note, 20% discount, $6M cap
- $250,000 already committed by an angel investor
- $350,000 still open
- Closes December 15

If you'd like to take part, please reply to me by **December 1** with the amount. I'm happy to talk it through before then.

Thank you for backing us,

[Your name]
</final_document>

The update comes to about 450 words. Two additions would make it stronger if you can get them before sending:

- **The number of hives paying for the app, and your churn.** This is your best answer to both the seasonality and the cheaper competitor.
- **What the bridge gets you to,** such as a revenue level, a customer count or the next raise. Investors putting in money will want to know what it buys.
